children.text: EINLEITUNG (nidānam)
children.translated_text: INTRODUCTION (<s>nidāna</s>)

children.text: I
children.translated_text: I

children.text:
s(i)ddham*
niṣkrāntā anupasaṃpannāḥ samagraḥ saṃghaḥ saṃnipatitaḥ kiṃ saṃghasya karaṇīyam anāgatānām āyuṣmantaś chandaṃ pariśuddhiṃ cārocayata ārocite ca pravedayataḥ
children.translated_text: It is accomplished. Those who have gone forth but are not fully ordained [should leave]. The complete <s>Saṃgha</s> has assembled. What is the business of the <s>Saṃgha</s>? Venerable ones, announce the consent and purity of those not present, and report what has been announced.

children.text: nirgatam āyuṣmanto grīṣmād ekarātrono māsaḥ saikarātrās trayo māsā avaśiṣṭāḥ /
children.translated_text: Venerable ones, one night of the summer [month] has passed. Three months with one night remain.

children.text: II
children.translated_text: II

children.text:
ākramate jarāmaraṇaṃ pralujyati śāstuḥ śāsanam
vilupyate jīvitendriyaṃ / nirgacchati saddharmaḥ sīdati pratip...ir jāyate śaithilyaṃ / vivṛyante apāyadvārā / pithīyante amṛtadvārā cchidyate dharmasetur bhidyate dharmapotaḥ saṃsīdati dharmaplavo / niśāmyate dharmolkā /
children.translated_text: Old age and death encroach. The teaching of the Master is crumbling. The life-faculty is being destroyed. The true <s>Dharma</s> is departing. The practice is declining. Slackness arises. The doors to the lower realms are opened. The doors to the deathless are shut. The bridge of <s>Dharma</s> is being broken. The boat of <s>Dharma</s> is shattered. The raft of <s>Dharma</s> is sinking. The torch of <s>Dharma</s> is dimming.

children.text: utpāṭyate dharmavṛkṣaḥ prapatati dharmadhvajaḥ ucchrapyate māradhvajaḥ śuṣyate dharmasamudro vikīryate jñānasumerur astaṃgacchaṃti vādiśārdūlā + + karṇādhārāḥ satpathopadeśakāḥ
children.translated_text: The tree of <s>Dharma</s> is being uprooted. The banner of <s>Dharma</s> is falling. The banner of <s>Māra</s> is being raised. The ocean of <s>Dharma</s> is drying up. The <s>Sumeru</s> of knowledge is scattered. The tiger-like debaters [are vanishing]... the helmsmen, the teachers of the right path.

children.text: acirād dhi manuṣyāṇāṃ mṛgasaṃjñā [bh]. .i + + + ti tasmāt sarvair āyuṣmadbhir udvignaiḥ saṃvegam āpannaiḥ tasyānuttaradaśabaladharadharmarājacakravartinaḥ paurāṇasucaritakarmavipākanirjātasya mṛṣāvādapaiśunyapāruṣyābaddhapralāpavivarjitasya satyānuvartivaca[na] + + + māsāvavādānuśāsanaṃ śrotavyam
children.translated_text: For soon among humans, the perception of animals [will prevail]... Therefore, all venerable ones, being alarmed and having attained a sense of urgency, should listen to the fortnightly instruction and admonition of that unsurpassed <s>Dharma</s>-king, the supreme sovereign bearing the ten powers, whose speech, born from the ripened fruit of former good conduct, is free from falsehood, slander, harsh speech, and idle chatter, and accords with truth.

children.text: apramādenāyuṣmadbhir yogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ apramādādhigatā hi tathāgatānām arhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ bodhir ye cāpy anye kuśalā dharmā bodhapakṣyāḥ //
children.translated_text: Venerable ones, you should practice with diligence. For the awakening of the <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the <s>Arhat</s>s, the Perfectly Awakened Ones, was attained through diligence, as were all other wholesome <s>dharma</s>s pertaining to awakening.

children.text: III
children.translated_text: III

children.text:
PrMoSū_Einl.III.1:
  śāsayatīti hi śāstraṃ proktaṃ samyak ca śāsayaty eṣaḥ
  mokṣāya prātimokṣas tasmāc chāstraṃ pravaram etat (1) /
children.translated_text: That which instructs is called a teaching (<s>śāstra</s>), and this one instructs rightly. Because [it leads] to liberation, [it is called] <s>Prātimokṣa</s>. Therefore this is the supreme teaching. (1)

children.text:
PrMoSū_Einl.III.2:
  kāryākāryam avācyaṃ vācyaṃ yac caiva bhikṣuṇā yuktam
  tad iha nikhilena muninā prakāśitaṃ prātimokṣe 'smiṃ 2 /
children.translated_text: What is to be done and not to be done, what is not to be said and what is to be said, and whatever is proper for a <s>bhikṣu</s> — all this has been fully revealed by the Sage in this <s>Prātimokṣa</s>. (2)

children.text:
PrMoSū_Einl.III.3:
  duścaritād vārayati trividhāt trividhe śubhe niyojayati /
  bṛṃhayati kuśalapakṣaṃ kṣapayati doṣāṃ guṇasapatnāṃ 3 /
children.translated_text: It restrains from the threefold misconduct, establishes in the threefold good. It strengthens the side of the wholesome and eliminates faults that are enemies of virtues. (3)

children.text:
PrMoSū_Einl.III.4:
  mithyājīvam anāryaṃ vināśayati durgatipraṇetāram
  svargāpavargamārgaṃ viśodhayati cānupūrveṇa 4 /
children.translated_text: It destroys wrong livelihood, which is ignoble and leads to the lower realms. And it purifies step by step the path to heaven and liberation. (4)

children.text:
PrMoSū_Einl.III.5:
  yāvat sthāsyaty eṣaḥ prakāśitas tena lokanāthena /
  tāvat sthāsyati dharmo loke 'smiṃ śākyasiṃhasya 5 /
children.translated_text: As long as this [<s>Prātimokṣa</s>], taught by that Lord of the World, will endure, so long will the <s>Dharma</s> of the Lion of the <s>Śākya</s>s endure in this world. (5)

children.text:
PrMoSū_Einl.III.6:
  tasmād ātmahitārthaṃ sthityarthaṃ śāsanasya caiva ciram /
  śṛṇuta muhūrtam avahitā vakṣyāmi prātimokṣam aham 6 / //
children.translated_text: Therefore, for the sake of your own welfare and for the long duration of the teaching, listen attentively for a moment — I shall recite the <s>Prātimokṣa</s>. (6)

children.text: IV
children.translated_text: IV

children.text:
śṛṇotu bhadantaḥ saṃghaḥ adya saṃghasya poṣathaḥ pāṃcadaśikaḥ sacet saṃghasya prāptakālaḥ kṣamate ājñā ca saṃghasya yat samagraḥ saṃgho 'dya poṣathaṃ kuryāt prātimokṣasūtram uddiśed eṣā jñaptiḥ poṣathaṃ vayam āyuṣmaṃtaḥ kariṣyāmaḥ prātimokṣasūtram uddekṣyāmas tat sarve saṃtaḥ śṛṇuta sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasikuruta
yasya vaḥ syāt saty āpattiḥ sāviṣkartavyā asatyām āpattau tūṣṇīṃ bhavitavyaṃ tūṣṇīṃbhāvena vayam āyuṣmantaḥ pariśuddhā iti vedayiṣyāmo yathā ca pratyekapṛṣṭasya bhikṣor vyākaraṇaṃ bhavaty evam evaivaṃrūpāyāṃ bhikṣupariṣadi yāvat trir apy anuśrāvaṇā bhavati /
yaḥ punar bhikṣur evaṃrūpāyāṃ bhikṣupariṣadi yāvat trir apy anuśrāvyamāṇe smaraṃ satīm āpattiṃ nāviṣkaroti saṃprajānamṛṣāvādo 'sya bhavati saṃprajānamṛṣāvādas tv āyuṣmanta antarāyiko dharma ity uktaṃ bhagavatā tasmād āpannena bhikṣuṇā viśuddhiprekṣiṇā smaratā satī āpattir āviṣkartavyā / āviṣkṛtvāsya phāṣaṃ bhavati nānāviṣkṛtvā //
children.translated_text: Let the venerable <s>Saṃgha</s> listen. Today is the <s>Saṃgha</s>'s <s>poṣatha</s> (observance day), the fifteenth. If the time has come for the <s>Saṃgha</s>, and if it is the instruction and consent of the <s>Saṃgha</s>, let the complete <s>Saṃgha</s> today perform the <s>poṣatha</s> and recite the <s>Prātimokṣa Sūtra</s>. This is the motion. Venerable ones, we shall perform the <s>poṣatha</s> and recite the <s>Prātimokṣa Sūtra</s>. Let all who are present listen well and pay close attention. Whoever has committed an offense must confess it. One who has committed no offense should remain silent. By your silence, venerable ones, we shall understand that you are pure. And just as a <s>bhikṣu</s> who is individually questioned must answer,

children.text: V
children.translated_text: V

children.text: uddiṣṭaṃ mayāyuṣmantaḥ prātimokṣasūtroddeśasya nidānaṃ / tatrāham āyuṣmataḥ pṛcchāmi kaccit sthātra pariśuddhā dvir api trir api pṛcchāmi kaccit sthātra pariśuddhā(ḥ) pariśuddhā atrāyuṣmanto yasmāt tūṣṇīm evam evāhaṃ dhārayāmi //
children.translated_text: I have recited, venerable ones, the introduction to the recitation of the <s>Prātimokṣa Sūtra</s>. Therein I ask the venerable ones: Are you pure in this matter? A second time and a third time I ask: Are you pure in this matter? The venerable ones are pure in this matter, since they are silent. Thus do I understand it.

children.text: I. pārājikā dharmāḥ
children.translated_text: I. <s>Pārājika</s> offenses (offenses entailing defeat)

children.text:
PrMoSū_Pār.0:
ime punar āyuṣmantaś catvāraḥ pārājikā dharmā anvardhamāsaṃ prātimokṣasūtroddeśam āgacchanti /
children.translated_text: Now, venerable ones, these four <s>pārājika</s> offenses come up for recitation in the <s>Prātimokṣa Sūtra</s> every half-month.

children.text:
PrMoSū_Pār.1:
yaḥ punar bhikṣur bhikṣubhiḥ sārdhaṃ śikṣāsāmīcisamāpannaḥ śikṣām apratyākhyā(ya śi)kṣādaurbalyaṃ vānāviṣkṛtvā maithunaṃ dharmaṃ pratiṣeveta antatas tīryagyonigatayāpi sārdham ayaṃ bhikṣuḥ pārājiko bhavaty asaṃvāsyaḥ 1
children.translated_text: 1. Whatever <s>bhikṣu</s>, having undertaken the training together with <s>bhikṣu</s>s and having reached conformity with the training, without having renounced the training or without having declared the weakness of his training, should engage in sexual intercourse, even with a female animal — this <s>bhikṣu</s> is defeated (<s>pārājika</s>) and is no longer in communion.

children.text:
PrMoSū_Pār.2:
yaḥ punar bhikṣur adattaṃ steyasaṃkhyātam ādadyād yathārūpeṇādattādānena rājā hy enaṃ gṛhītvā hanyād vā badhnīyād vā pravāsayed vā evaṃ cainaṃ vadec coro 'si bālo 'si mūḍho 'si steyo 'sīty evaṃrūpaṃ bhikṣur adattam ādadānaḥ pārājiko bhavaty asaṃvāsyaḥ 2
children.translated_text: 2. Whatever <s>bhikṣu</s> should take what is not given, in a manner that constitutes theft, such that a king, having seized him, would execute him, bind him, or banish him, saying "You are a thief, you are a fool, you are an idiot, you are a robber" — a <s>bhikṣu</s> who takes what is not given in such a manner is defeated (<s>pārājika</s>) and is no longer in communion.

children.text:
PrMoSū_Pār.3:
yaḥ punar bhikṣur manuṣyaṃ svahastena saṃcintya jīvitād vyaparopayec chastraṃ vainam ādhārayec chastrādhārakaṃ vāsya paryeṣayed evaṃ vainaṃ vaded dhambhoḥ puruṣa kiṃ tavānena pāpakena durjīvitena mṛtaṃ te jīvitād varam iti cittānumataṃ cittasaṃkalpitam anekaparyāyeṇa maraṇāya samādāpayen maraṇavarṇaṃ vāsyānusaṃvarṇayet sa ca tenopakrameṇa kālaṃ kuryād ayam api bhikṣuḥ pārājiko bhavaty asaṃvāsyaḥ 3
children.translated_text: 3. Whatever <s>bhikṣu</s> should intentionally deprive a human being of life with his own hand, or should provide a weapon, or should seek a weapon-provider, or should address him thus: "Come, good man, what use to you is this evil, miserable life? Death is better for you than life" — with such mental intent and mental resolve, should in various ways incite to death or praise the advantage of dying, and if that person should die by that means — this <s>bhikṣu</s> too is defeated (<s>pārājika</s>) and is no longer in communion.

children.text:
PrMoSū_Pār.4:
yaḥ punar bhikṣur anabhijāna(n)n aparijānann uttarimanuṣyadharmam alamāryaviśeṣādhigamaṃ jñānaṃ vā darśanaṃ vā pratijānīyāj jānāmīti paśyāmīti so 'pareṇa samayena samanuyujyamāno vā asamanuyujyamāno vā evaṃ vaded ajānamāno 'ham avocaṃ jānāmīty apaśyann avocaṃ paśyāmīti tucchaṃ mṛṣā vilapitam anyatrābhimānād ayam api bhikṣuḥ pārājiko bhavaty asaṃvāsyaḥ 4 //
children.translated_text: 4. Whatever <s>bhikṣu</s>, without knowing or realizing, should claim a superhuman state, a knowledge or vision worthy of the noble ones and constituting a superior attainment, [saying] "I know, I see" — and at a later time, whether questioned or not questioned, should say: "Not knowing, I said 'I know'; not seeing, I said 'I see' — it was empty, false, idle talk," except through overestimation — this <s>bhikṣu</s> too is defeated (<s>pārājika</s>) and is no longer in communion.

children.text: uddiṣṭā mayāyuṣmantaś catvāraḥ pārājikā dharmā yeṣāṃ bhikṣur anyatamānyatamaṃ dharmam āpanno na labhate bhikṣubhiḥ sārdhaṃ saṃvāsaṃ vā saṃbhogaṃ vā yathā pūrvaṃ tathā paścāt pārājiko bhavaty asaṃvāsyaḥ tatrāham āyuṣmataḥ pṛcchāmi kaccit sthātra pariśuddhā dvir api trir api pṛcchāmi kaccit sthātra pa(riśuddhāḥ pariśuddhā a)trāyuṣmanto yasmā(t) tūṣṇīm evam evāhaṃ dhārayāmi //
children.translated_text: I have recited, venerable ones, the four <s>pārājika</s> offenses. A <s>bhikṣu</s> who has committed any one of these offenses no longer has communion or shared enjoyment with the <s>bhikṣu</s>s; as before, so afterwards — he is defeated (<s>pārājika</s>) and is no longer in communion. Therein I ask the venerable ones: Are you pure in this matter? A second time and a third time I ask: Are you pure in this matter? The venerable ones are pure in this matter, since they are silent. Thus do I understand it.

children.text: II. saṃghāvaśeṣā dharmāḥ
children.translated_text: II. <s>Saṃghāvaśeṣa</s> offenses (offenses entailing a formal meeting of the Saṃgha)

children.text:
PrMoSū_SA.0:
ime punar āyuṣmantas trayodaśa saṃghāvaśeṣā dharmā anvardhamāsaṃ prātimokṣasūtroddeśam āgacchanti /
children.translated_text: Now, venerable ones, these thirteen <s>saṃghāvaśeṣa</s> offenses come up for recitation in the <s>Prātimokṣa Sūtra</s> every half-month.

children.text:
PrMoSū_SA.1:
saṃcintya śukravisargo 'nyatra svapnāntarāt saṃghāvaśeṣaḥ 1
children.translated_text: 1. Intentional emission of semen, except during a dream, is a <s>saṃghāvaśeṣa</s> offense.

children.text:
PrMoSū_SA.2:
yaḥ punar bhikṣur udīrṇavipariṇatena cittena mātṛgrāmeṇa sārdhaṃ kāyasaṃsargaṃ samāpadyeta hastagrahaṇaṃ vā veṇīgrahaṇaṃ vā anyatamānyatamasya vāṅgajātasyāmarśanaṃ parāmarśanaṃ vā saṃghāvaśeṣaḥ 2
children.translated_text: 2. Whatever <s>bhikṣu</s>, with an excited and perverted mind, should come into bodily contact with a woman — whether grasping her hand, or grasping her hair, or touching or fondling any part of her body — this is a <s>saṃghāvaśeṣa</s> offense.

children.text:
PrMoSū_SA.3:
yaḥ punar bhikṣur udīrṇavipariṇatena cittena mātṛgrāmaṃ duṣṭhulayā vācā ābhāṣeta pāpikayā asabhyayā maithunopasaṃhitayā yathāpi tad yuvā yuvatīm iti saṃghāvaśeṣaḥ 3
children.translated_text: 3. Whatever <s>bhikṣu</s>, with an excited and perverted mind, should address a woman with coarse, wicked, indecent words connected with sexual intercourse, just as a young man [would address] a young woman — this is a <s>saṃghāvaśeṣa</s> offense.

children.text:
PrMoSū_SA.4:
yaḥ punar bhikṣur udīrṇavipariṇatena cittena mātṛgrāmasyāntike ātmanaḥ kāyaparicaryāyā varṇaṃ bhāṣeta eṣāgry(ā) bhagini paricaryāṇāṃ ya(n) mādṛśaṃ bhikṣuṃ śīlavantaṃ kalyāṇadharmāṇaṃ brahmacāriṇam ane(na) dharmeṇa paricared yaduta maithunopasaṃhitena saṃghāvaśeṣaḥ 4
children.translated_text: 4. Whatever <s>bhikṣu</s>, with an excited and perverted mind, in the presence of a woman, should praise the service of his own body [saying]: "This, sister, is the foremost of services — that one should serve a <s>bhikṣu</s> like me, who is virtuous, of good character, and a celibate, with this [sexual] act" — this is a <s>saṃghāvaśeṣa</s> offense.

children.text:
PrMoSū_SA.5:
yaḥ punar bhikṣuḥ saṃcāritraṃ samāpadyeta striyā vā puruṣamatena puruṣasya vā strīmatena jāyātvena vā jāritvena vā antatas tatkṣaṇam api saṃghāvaśeṣaḥ 5
children.translated_text: 5. Whatever <s>bhikṣu</s> should act as a go-between — conveying a woman's intention to a man or a man's intention to a woman, whether for marriage or for a liaison, even for a single occasion — this is a <s>saṃghāvaśeṣa</s> offense.

children.text:
PrMoSū_SA.6:
svayācitāṃ bhikṣuṇā kuṭiṃ kārayatā asvāmikām ātmoddeśikāṃ prāmāṇikā kuṭiḥ kārayitavyā tatredaṃ kuṭipramāṇaṃ dīrghato dvādaśa vitastayaḥ sugatavitastyā tīryak saptāntaratas
tena bhikṣuṇā bhikṣavo 'bhinetavyā vāstu deśayitum abhinītair bhikṣubhir vāstu deśayitavyam anārambhaṃ saparākramaṃ
sārambhe ced bhikṣur vāstuny aparākrame svayācitāṃ kuṭiṃ kārayamāṇa asvāmikām ātmoddeśikāṃ bhikṣ(ū)n nābhinayed vāstu deśayituṃ pramāṇaṃ vātikramet saṃghāvaśeṣaḥ 6
children.translated_text:
<s>PrMoSū_SA</s>.6:
When a <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) is having a hut built by his own begging, without an owner, for his own use, the hut to be built must be of proper measure. Here, this is the measure of the hut: twelve <s>vitastis</s> (spans) in length by the <s>Sugata</s>'s span, seven in breadth on the interior.
That <s>bhikṣu</s> must bring <s>bhikṣus</s> to inspect the site. The <s>bhikṣus</s> who have been brought must inspect a site that is free from harm to living beings and has adequate access.
If a <s>bhikṣu</s>, on a site with harm to living beings and without adequate access, while having a hut built by his own begging, without an owner, for his own use, does not bring <s>bhikṣus</s> to inspect the site, or exceeds the measure — <s>saṃghāvaśeṣa</s> (offense requiring formal meeting of the <s>Saṅgha</s>). 6

children.text:
PrMoSū_SA.7:
m(a)hallakaṃ bhikṣuṇā vihāraṃ kārayatā sasvāmikam ātmoddeśikaṃ tena bhikṣuṇā bhikṣavo 'bhineta(vyā vā)stu deśayitum abhinītair bhikṣubhir vāstu deśayitavyam anāraṃbha(ṃ) saparākramaṃ
sāra(ṃ)bhe ced bhi(kṣur vāstu)ny aparākrame mahallakaṃ vihāraṃ kārayamāṇaḥ sasvāmikam ātmoddeśikaṃ bhikṣ(ū)n nābhinayed vāstudeśanāyai saṃghāvaśeṣaḥ 7
children.translated_text:
<s>PrMoSū_SA</s>.7:
When a <s>bhikṣu</s> is having a large monastery built, with an owner, for his own use, that <s>bhikṣu</s> must bring <s>bhikṣus</s> to inspect the site. The <s>bhikṣus</s> who have been brought must inspect a site that is free from harm to living beings and has adequate access.
If a <s>bhikṣu</s>, on a site with harm to living beings and without adequate access, while having a large monastery built, with an owner, for his own use, does not bring <s>bhikṣus</s> for site inspection — <s>saṃghāvaśeṣa</s>. 7

children.text:
PrMoSū_SA.8:
yaḥ punar bhikṣur duṣṭo doṣād apratītaḥ śuddhaṃ bhikṣum an(āpa)nna(m) amūlakena pārājikena dharmeṇānudhvaṃsayed apy evainaṃ brahmacaryāc cyāvayeyam iti
tasya sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca samanuyujyamānasya samanugāhyamānasya amūlaṃ caiva tad adhikaraṇaṃ bhaved bhikṣuś cānudhvaṃsayitā doṣe pratitiṣṭhed doṣeṇ(āvocam iti) saṃghāvaśeṣ(aḥ) 8
children.translated_text:
<s>PrMoSū_SA</s>.8:
If a <s>bhikṣu</s>, angry, hostile, and displeased, charges a pure <s>bhikṣu</s> who has not committed an offense with a baseless <s>pārājika</s> (defeat) offense, thinking 'Perhaps I may thereby cause him to fall from the holy life' —
when that [accuser], being properly questioned and investigated, and [it is found that] the charge is baseless, and the <s>bhikṣu</s> who made the accusation admits to the fault, [saying] 'I spoke out of malice' — <s>saṃghāvaśeṣa</s>. 8

children.text:
PrMoSū_SA.9:
yaḥ punar bhikṣur duṣṭo doṣād apratītaḥ anyathābhāgīyasyādhikaraṇasya kaṃcid eva leśamātraṃ dharmam upādāya apārājikaṃ bhikṣuṃ pārājikena dharmeṇānudhvaṃsayed apy evainaṃ brahmacaryāc cyāvayeyam iti
tasya sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca samanuyujyamānasya samanugāhyamānasya anyathābhāgi tad adhikaraṇaṃ bhaved anyathābhāgīnaś cādhikaraṇāt kaścid eva leśamātro dharma upādatto bhaved bhikṣuś cānudhvaṃsayitā doṣe pratitiṣṭhed doṣeṇāvocam iti saṃghavaśeṣa(ḥ) 9
children.translated_text:
<s>PrMoSū_SA</s>.9:
If a <s>bhikṣu</s>, angry, hostile, and displeased, seizing upon some mere fragment of a matter from a case of a different nature, charges a non-<s>pārājika</s> <s>bhikṣu</s> with a <s>pārājika</s> offense, thinking 'Perhaps I may thereby cause him to fall from the holy life' —
when that [accuser], being properly questioned and investigated, and [it is found that] the charge pertains to a case of a different nature, and some mere fragment of a matter has been seized from a case of a different nature, and the <s>bhikṣu</s> who made the accusation admits to the fault, [saying] 'I spoke out of malice' — <s>saṃghāvaśeṣa</s>. 9

children.text:
PrMoSū_SA.10:
yaḥ punar bhikṣuḥ samagrasya saṃghasya bhedāya parākramed bhedasaṃvartanīyaṃ vādhikaraṇaṃ samādāya vigṛhya tiṣṭhet sa bhikṣur bhikṣubhir evaṃ syād vacanīyo mā tvam āyuṣmaṃ samagrasya saṃghasya bhedāya parākrama mā bhedasaṃvartanīyam adhikaraṇaṃ samādāya vigṛhya sth(ā)ḥ
sametv āyuṣmaṃ sārdhaṃ saṃghena samagro hi saṃghaḥ sahitaḥ saṃmodamāna avivadamāna ekāgra ekoddeśa ekakṣīrodakībhūtaḥ sukhaṃ phāṣaṃ viharati niḥsṛja tvam āyuṣmaṃ saṃghabhedakaraṃ vastu /
evaṃ cet sa bhikṣur bhikṣubhir ucyamānas tad eva vastu samādāya vigṛhya tiṣṭhen na pratiniḥsṛjet sa bhikṣur bhikṣubhir yāvat trir api samanuśāsitavyas tasya vastunaḥ pratiniḥsargāya sa yāvat trir api samanuśiṣyamāṇas tad vastu pratiniḥsṛjed ity evaṃ kuśalaṃ no cet pratiniḥsṛjet saṃghāvaśeṣaḥ 10
children.translated_text:
<s>PrMoSū_SA</s>.10:
If a <s>bhikṣu</s> strives for the schism of a united <s>Saṅgha</s>, or taking up a matter conducive to schism, persists in holding to it, that <s>bhikṣu</s> should be addressed by the <s>bhikṣus</s> thus: 'Let the venerable one (<s>āyuṣmat</s>) not strive for the schism of a united <s>Saṅgha</s>, nor take up a matter conducive to schism and persist in holding to it.
Let the venerable one be united with the <s>Saṅgha</s>, for the <s>Saṅgha</s> that is united, harmonious, rejoicing together, not quarreling, of one mind, of one recitation, blended like milk and water, dwells in happiness and ease. Let the venerable one relinquish the matter that causes schism in the <s>Saṅgha</s>.'
If that <s>bhikṣu</s>, when so addressed by the <s>bhikṣus</s>, takes up and persists in holding to that very matter and does not relinquish it, that <s>bhikṣu</s> must be formally admonished by the <s>bhikṣus</s> up to three times for the relinquishing of that matter. If, when being so admonished up to three times, he relinquishes that matter — thus it is well. If he does not relinquish it — <s>saṃghāvaśeṣa</s>. 10

children.text:
PrMoSū_SA.11:
tasya ced bhikṣor bhikṣavaḥ syur anuvartino vyagravādina eko vā dvau vā saṃbahulā vā te tāṃ bhikṣūn evaṃ vadeyur mā yūyam āyuṣmaṃta itthaṃnāmānaṃ bhikṣum atra vastuniḥ kiṃcid vadantu tat kasmād dhetor dharmavādī caiṣa bhikṣur vinayavādī ca asmākaṃ caiṣa cchandaṃ ca ruciṃ cādāyānuvyāharati / jānaṃ caiṣa bhikṣur bhāṣate nājānaṃ yac cāsya bhikṣo rocate ca kṣamate ca asmākam api tad rocate ca kṣamate ca /
te bhikṣavo bhikṣubhir evaṃ syur vacanīyāḥ naiṣa bhikṣur dharmavādī na vinayavādī adharmaṃ caiṣo 'vinayaṃ cādāya vigṛhyānuvyāharati (niḥ)sṛja(ṃ)tv āyuṣmantaḥ saṃghabhedānuvartitāṃ vyagravāditāṃ samagro hi saṃghaḥ sahitaḥ saṃmodamāna avivadamāna ekāgra ekoddeśa ekakṣīrodakībhūtaḥ sukhaṃ phāṣaṃ viharati
evaṃ cet te bhikṣavo bhikṣubhir uc(y)amānās tad eva vastu samādāya vigṛhya tiṣṭheyur na pratiniḥsṛjeyus te bhikṣavo bhikṣubhir yāvat t(ri)r api samanuśāsitavyās tasya vastunaḥ pratiniḥsargāya te yā(vat tr)ir api samanuśiṣyamāṇās tad vastu pratiniḥsṛjeyur ity evaṃ kuśalaṃ (no cet pra)t(i)niḥsṛjeyuḥ saṃghāvaśeṣaḥ 11
children.translated_text:
<s>PrMoSū_SA</s>.11:
If that <s>bhikṣu</s> has <s>bhikṣus</s> who are his followers and partisans, whether one, two, or many, and those [followers] address those <s>bhikṣus</s> thus: 'Let the venerable ones not say anything to this <s>bhikṣu</s> named so-and-so regarding this matter. For what reason? This <s>bhikṣu</s> speaks <s>Dharma</s> and speaks <s>Vinaya</s>. He takes up and articulates what is agreeable and pleasing to us. This <s>bhikṣu</s> speaks knowingly, not unknowingly. Whatever is pleasing and acceptable to this <s>bhikṣu</s> is pleasing and acceptable to us as well.'
Those <s>bhikṣus</s> should be addressed by the [other] <s>bhikṣus</s> thus: 'This <s>bhikṣu</s> does not speak <s>Dharma</s>, nor does he speak <s>Vinaya</s>. He takes up and articulates what is contrary to <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s> in a disputatious manner. Let the venerable ones relinquish the following of a schismatic and the partisanship. For the <s>Saṅgha</s> that is united, harmonious, rejoicing together, not quarreling, of one mind, of one recitation, blended like milk and water, dwells in happiness and ease.'
If those <s>bhikṣus</s>, when so addressed by the [other] <s>bhikṣus</s>, take up and persist in holding to that very matter and do not relinquish it, those <s>bhikṣus</s> must be formally admonished by the [other] <s>bhikṣus</s> up to three times for the relinquishing of that matter. If, when being so admonished up to three times, they relinquish that matter — thus it is well. If they do not relinquish it — <s>saṃghāvaśeṣa</s>. 11

children.text:
PrMoSū_SA.12:
bhikṣuḥ punar anyatamaṃ grāmaṃ vā nigamaṃ vopaniḥś(ri)tya viharet sa ca syāt kuladūṣakaḥ pā(pa)samācāraḥ tasya kulāni duṣṭāni dṛśyeran vā śrūyeran vā prajñāyeran vā pāpakāś ca tasya samācārā dṛśyera(n) vā śrūyera(n) vā prajñāyeran vā kuladūṣakaś ca syāt pāpasamācā(raḥ)
sa bhikṣur bhikṣubhir evaṃ syād vacanīyaḥ āyuṣmāṃ kuladūṣakaḥ pā(pasamā)cāras tasya te kulāni duṣṭāni dṛśyante 'pi śrūyante 'pi prajñāyante 'pi pāpak(ā)ś ca te sam(ācārā d)ṛ(ś)y(a)nte 'pi śrūyante 'pi prajñāyante 'pi kuladūṣakaś cāyuṣmāṃ pāpasamācāraḥ prakramatv ā(yu)ṣmā(ṃ) asmād āvāsād alaṃ tavehoṣitena
evaṃ cet sa bhikṣur bhikṣubhir ucyamānas tān bhikṣūn evaṃ vadec chandagāmina āyuṣmanto bhikṣavo dveṣagāmino bhayagāmino mo(ha)gāmino yatra hi nāma tādṛśīm evāpattim āpannān ekatyāṃ bhikṣūṃ pravāsayanty ekatyāṃ bhikṣūn na pravāsayanti
sa bhikṣur bhikṣubhir evaṃ syād vacanīyaḥ neme bhikṣavaś chandagāmin(o na) d(v)eṣagāmino na bhayagāmino na mohagāmina api tv āyuṣmān eva kuladūṣakaḥ pāpasamācāraḥ tasya te kulāni duṣṭāni dṛśyante 'pi śrūyante 'pi prajñāya(n)t(e) 'p(i) p(ā)pakāś ca te samācārā dṛśyante 'pi śrūyante 'pi prajñāyante 'pi kuladūṣakaś cāyuṣmān pāpasamācāraḥ niḥsṛjatv āyuṣmāṃś chandagāmi vacanaṃ dveṣagāmi bhayagāmi mohagāmi vacanaṃ
evaṃ cet sa bhikṣur bhikṣubhir ucyamānas tad eva vastu samādāya vigṛhya tiṣṭhen na pratiniḥsṛjet sa bhikṣur bhikṣubhir yāvat trir api samanuśāsitavyas tasya vastunaḥ pratiniḥsargāya sa yāvat trir api samanuśiṣyamāṇas tad vastu pratiniḥsṛjed ity evaṃ kuśalaṃ no cet pratiniḥsṛjet saṃghāvaśeṣaḥ 12
children.translated_text:
<s>PrMoSū_SA</s>.12:
If a <s>bhikṣu</s> lives in dependence upon a certain village or town, and he is a corrupter of families and of evil conduct, and his corrupted families are seen, heard of, or known, and his evil practices are seen, heard of, or known, and he is a corrupter of families and of evil conduct —
that <s>bhikṣu</s> should be addressed by the <s>bhikṣus</s> thus: 'The venerable one is a corrupter of families and of evil conduct. Your corrupted families are seen, heard of, and known. Your evil practices are seen, heard of, and known. The venerable one is a corrupter of families and of evil conduct. Let the venerable one depart from this dwelling. Enough of your residing here.'
If that <s>bhikṣu</s>, when so addressed by the <s>bhikṣus</s>, says to those <s>bhikṣus</s>: 'The venerable <s>bhikṣus</s> are acting out of favoritism, acting out of hostility, acting out of fear, acting out of delusion — since, indeed, for the very same offense, they banish some <s>bhikṣus</s> but do not banish others' —
that <s>bhikṣu</s> should be addressed by the <s>bhikṣus</s> thus: 'These <s>bhikṣus</s> are not acting out of favoritism, nor out of hostility, nor out of fear, nor out of delusion. Rather, it is the venerable one himself who is a corrupter of families and of evil conduct. Your corrupted families are seen, heard of, and known. Your evil practices are seen, heard of, and known. The venerable one is a corrupter of families and of evil conduct. Let the venerable one relinquish the speech of favoritism, hostility, fear, and delusion.'
If that <s>bhikṣu</s>, when so addressed by the <s>bhikṣus</s>, takes up and persists in holding to that very matter and does not relinquish it, that <s>bhikṣu</s> must be formally admonished by the <s>bhikṣus</s> up to three times for the relinquishing of that matter. If, when being so admonished up to three times, he relinquishes that matter — thus it is well. If he does not relinquish it — <s>saṃghāvaśeṣa</s>. 12

children.text: PrMoSū_SA.13:

bhikṣuḥ punar ihaikatyo durvacajātīyaḥ syāt sa uddeśaparyāpannaiḥ śikṣāpadair bhikṣubhiḥ saha dharmeṇa saha vinayenocyamāna ātmānam avacanīyaṃ kuryān mā mām āyuṣmantaḥ ki(ṃ)cid vadantu kalyāṇaṃ vā pāpakaṃ vā aham apy āyuṣmato na kiṃcid vakṣyāmi kalyāṇaṃ vā pāpakaṃ vā virama(n)tv āyuṣmanto madvacanād alaṃ vo m. + + ktena
children.translated_text: If a certain <s>bhikṣu</s> is of a difficult-to-admonish nature, and when addressed by <s>bhikṣus</s> in accordance with <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s> regarding the training rules included in the recitation (<s>uddeśa</s>), he makes himself unamenable to correction, [saying:] 'Let the venerable ones not say anything to me, whether good or bad. I too shall not say anything to the venerable ones, whether good or bad. Let the venerable ones desist from correcting me. Enough of your [attempts to instruct me]' —

children.text: sa bhikṣur bhikṣubhir evaṃ syād vacanīyo mā tvam āyuṣmann uddeśaparyāpannaiḥ śikṣāpadair bhikṣubhiḥ saha dharmeṇa saha vinayenocyamāna ātmānam avacanīyaṃ kārṣīr vacanīyam evāyuṣmān ātmānaṃ karotu āyuṣma(n)tam api bhikṣavo vakṣyanti saha dharmeṇa saha vinayena āyuṣmān api bhikṣūṃ vadatu saha dharmeṇa saha vinayena evaṃ saṃvṛddhā tasya bhagavataḥ pariṣad yadutānyonyavacanīyād anyonyāvavādād anyonyānuśāsanād anyonyāpattivyutthāpanān niḥsṛjatv āyuṣm(ā)n ātma(na) avacanīyakarmāntatāṃ
children.translated_text: that <s>bhikṣu</s> should be addressed by the <s>bhikṣus</s> thus: 'Let the venerable one, when addressed by <s>bhikṣus</s> in accordance with <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s> regarding the training rules included in the recitation, not make himself unamenable to correction. Let the venerable one rather make himself amenable to correction. The <s>bhikṣus</s> too will speak to the venerable one in accordance with <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>. Let the venerable one also speak to the <s>bhikṣus</s> in accordance with <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>. For thus the assembly of the <s>Bhagavat</s> grows — namely, through mutual correction, mutual admonition, mutual instruction, and mutual rehabilitation from offenses. Let the venerable one relinquish his act of making himself unamenable to correction.'

children.text: evaṃ cet sa bhikṣur bhikṣubhir ucyamānas (ta)d eva vastu samādāya vigṛhya tiṣṭhen na pratiniḥsṛjet sa bhikṣur bhikṣubhir yāvat trir (api) samanuśāsitavyas tasya vastunaḥ pratiniḥsargāya sa yāvat trir api samanuśiṣyamāṇas tad vastu pratiniḥsṛjed ity evaṃ kuśalaṃ no cet pratiniḥsṛjet saṃghāvaśeṣaḥ 13 //
children.translated_text: If that <s>bhikṣu</s>, when admonished by the <s>bhikṣus</s>, should seize upon that very matter and persist in disputing it and not relinquish it, that <s>bhikṣu</s> should be admonished by the <s>bhikṣus</s> up to three times for the relinquishment of that matter. If, being admonished up to three times, he relinquishes that matter — thus it is well. If he does not relinquish it — <s>Saṃghāvaśeṣa</s> 13.
<s>PrMoSū_SA</s>.13:

children.text: uddiṣṭā mayāyuṣmantas trayodaśa saṃghāvaśeṣā dharmā nava prathamāpattayaś catvāro yāvattṛtīyakā yeṣāṃ bhikṣur anyatamānyatamaṃ dharmam āpanno yāvatkālaṃ jānaṃ praticchādayati tāvatkālam akāmaṃ parivastavyaṃ bhavati / paryuṣitaparivāsitena bhikṣuṇā uttaraṃ saṃghe ṣaḍrātraṃ mānāpyaṃ cartavyaṃ bhavati cīrṇamānāpyo bhikṣur (ā)bṛhaṇāt pratibaddhaḥ kṛtānudharmo yatra syād viṃśatigaṇo bhikṣusaṃghas tatra sa bhikṣur ābṛhitavya ekenāpy ūno viṃśatigaṇo bhikṣusaṃghas taṃ bhikṣum ābṛhyāt sa ca bhikṣur anābṛhitas te ca bhikṣavo garhyā iyaṃ tatra sāmīciḥ tatrāham āyuṣmataḥ pṛcchāmi kaccit sthātra pariśuddhā dvir api trir api pṛcchāmi kaccit sthātra pariśuddhāḥ pariśuddhā atrāyuṣmanto yasmāt tūṣṇīm evam etad dhārayāmi // //
children.translated_text:
Venerable ones, the thirteen <s>Saṃghāvaśeṣa</s> (requiring formal meeting of the <s>Saṃgha</s>) offenses have been recited by me — nine involving initial offense and four involving up to the third [admonition]. For whichever of these offenses a <s>bhikṣu</s> has committed, for as long as he knowingly conceals it, for that long he must unwillingly undergo probation (<s>parivāsa</s>). A <s>bhikṣu</s> who has completed his probation must further undergo six nights of penance (<s>mānāpya</s>) before the <s>Saṃgha</s>. A <s>bhikṣu</s> who has completed the penance, having fulfilled the discipline, and being bound by [the need for] rehabilitation (<s>ābṛhaṇa</s>) — where there is a <s>bhikṣu-saṃgha</s> of at least twenty members, there that <s>bhikṣu</s> is to be rehabilitated. If even one is lacking from the twenty-member <s>bhikṣu-saṃgha</s> and they rehabilitate that <s>bhikṣu</s>, that <s>bhikṣu</s> is not rehabilitated and those <s>bhikṣus</s> are blameworthy. This is the proper procedure in this matter.
I ask the venerable ones: are you pure in this matter? A second and third time I ask: are you pure in this matter? The venerable ones are pure in this matter, since they remain silent. Thus I understand it.

children.text: III. aniyatau dharmau
children.translated_text: III. The <s>Aniyata</s> (Undetermined) Offenses

children.text:
PrMoSū_Aniy.0:
imau punar āyuṣmanto dvāv aniyatau dharmāv anvardhamāsaṃ prātimokṣasūtroddeśam āgacchataḥ //
children.translated_text: Venerable ones, these two <s>Aniyata</s> (undetermined) offenses come up for recitation in the <s>Prātimokṣasūtra</s> every half-month.

children.text:
PrMoSū_Aniy.1:
yaḥ punar bhikṣur mātṛgrāmeṇa sārdham ekaikena rahasi praticchanne āsane niṣadyāṃ kalpayed alaṃ gama(n)īyena taṃ ca śrāddheyavacanopāsikā trayāṇāṃ dharmāṇām anyatamānyatamena dharmeṇa vadet pārājikena vā saṃghāvaśeṣeṇa vā pātayantikena vā niṣadyāṃ bhikṣuḥ pratijānamānas trayāṇāṃ dharmāṇām anyatamānyatamena dharmeṇa kārayitavyaḥ pārājikena vā saṃghāvaśeṣeṇa vā pātayantikena vā yena yena dharmeṇa vā śrāddheyavacanopāsikā taṃ bhikṣuṃ vadet tena tena sa bhikṣuḥ k(ā)rayitavyaḥ ayaṃ dharmo 'niyataḥ 1
children.translated_text: If a <s>bhikṣu</s> should sit in private with a woman, alone, in a concealed and secluded seat suitable for [sexual] conduct, and a trustworthy female lay-follower (<s>upāsikā</s>) should accuse him of any one of three offenses — <s>Pārājika</s>, or <s>Saṃghāvaśeṣa</s>, or <s>Pātayantikā</s> — that <s>bhikṣu</s>, confessing the sitting, should be dealt with according to whichever of the three offenses applies: <s>Pārājika</s>, or <s>Saṃghāvaśeṣa</s>, or <s>Pātayantikā</s>. According to whichever offense the trustworthy female lay-follower accuses that <s>bhikṣu</s>, he should be dealt with accordingly. This is an <s>Aniyata</s> offense 1.

children.text:
PrMoSū_Aniy.2:
na ca rahasi praticchanne āsane niṣadyāṃ kalpayen nāla(ṃ) gamanīyena api tu taṃ m(ā)tṛgrāmaṃ duṣṭhulayā vācā ābhāṣeta pāpikayā asabhyayā maithunopasaṃhitayā taṃ ca śrāddheyavacanopāsikā dvayor dharmayor anyatamānyatamena dharmeṇa vadet saṃghāvaśeṣeṇa vā pātayantikena vā niṣadyāṃ bhikṣuḥ pratijānamāno dvayor dharmayor anyatamānyatamena dharmeṇa kārayitavyaḥ saṃghāvaśeṣeṇa vā pā(t)ayantikena vā yena yena dharmeṇa vā śrāddheyavacanopāsikā taṃ bhikṣuṃ vadet tena tena sa bhikṣuḥ kārayitavyaḥ ayam api dharmo 'niyataḥ 2 /
children.translated_text: [If] the seat is not concealed or secluded, not suitable for [sexual] conduct, but the <s>bhikṣu</s> addresses that woman with lewd, evil, unseemly speech connected with sexual intercourse, and a trustworthy female lay-follower should accuse him of either of two offenses — <s>Saṃghāvaśeṣa</s> or <s>Pātayantikā</s> — that <s>bhikṣu</s>, confessing the sitting, should be dealt with according to whichever of the two offenses applies: <s>Saṃghāvaśeṣa</s> or <s>Pātayantikā</s>. According to whichever offense the trustworthy female lay-follower accuses that <s>bhikṣu</s>, he should be dealt with accordingly. This is an <s>Aniyata</s> offense 2.

children.text: uddiṣṭau mayāyuṣma(n)to dvāv aniyatau dharmau tatrāham āyuṣmataḥ pṛcchāmi kaccit sthātra pariśuddhā dvir api trir api pṛcchāmi kaccit sthātra pariśuddhāḥ pariśuddhā atrāyuṣmanto (yasmā)t tūṣṇīm evam etad dhārayāmi (// //)
children.translated_text: Venerable ones, the two <s>Aniyata</s> (undetermined) offenses have been recited by me. I ask the venerable ones: are you pure in this matter? A second and third time I ask: are you pure in this matter? The venerable ones are pure in this matter, since they remain silent. Thus I understand it.

children.text: IV. niḥsargikāḥ pātayantikā dharmāḥ
children.translated_text: IV. <s>Niḥsargikā Pātayantikā</s> (Offenses Requiring Forfeiture and Confession) Offenses

children.text:
PrMoSū_NP.0:
ime puna(r ā)yuṣmantas triṃśan niḥsargikāḥ pātayantikā dharmā anvardhamāsaṃ prātimokṣasūtroddeśam āgacchanti //
children.translated_text: Venerable ones, these thirty <s>Niḥsargikā Pātayantikā</s> (forfeiture and confession) offenses come up for recitation in the <s>Prātimokṣasūtra</s> every half-month.

children.text:
PrMoSū_NP.1:
niṣṭhitacīvareṇa bhikṣuṇā uddhṛte kaṭhine daśāhaparamam atiriktaṃ cīvaraṃ dhārayitavyaṃ tata uttaraṃ dhārayen niḥsargikā pātayantikā 1
children.translated_text: When a <s>bhikṣu</s>'s robe-making is finished and the <s>kaṭhina</s> (robe-ceremony) privilege has been removed, an extra robe may be kept for at most ten days. Should he keep it beyond that — <s>Niḥsargikā Pātayantikā</s> 1.

children.text:
PrMoSū_NP.2:
niṣṭhitacīvaro bhikṣur uddhṛte kaṭhine ekarātram api trayāṇāṃ cīvarāṇām anyatamānyatamasmāc cīvarād vipravased anyatra saṃghasaṃmatyā niḥsargikā pātayantikā 2
children.translated_text: When a <s>bhikṣu</s>'s robe-making is finished and the <s>kaṭhina</s> privilege has been removed, if he should be separated for even one night from any one of his three robes, except with the consent of the <s>Saṃgha</s> — <s>Niḥsargikā Pātayantikā</s> 2.

children.text:
PrMoSū_NP.3:
niṣṭhitacīvarasya bhikṣor uddhṛte kaṭhine utpadyetākālacīvaram āk(ā)ṃkṣamāṇena tena bhikṣuṇā pratigṛhītavyaṃ pratigṛhya sacet paripūryeta kṣipram eva kṛ(tvā) dhārayitavyaṃ no cet paripūryeta māsaparamaṃ tena bhikṣuṇā tac cīvaram upanikṣi(ptavyaṃ) satyā(ṃ) cīvarapratyāśāyām ūnasya vā paripūryārthaṃ tata uttaram upanikṣipen niḥsargikā pātaya(n)tikā 3
children.translated_text: When a <s>bhikṣu</s>'s robe-making is finished and the <s>kaṭhina</s> privilege has been removed, if out-of-season robe-cloth should arise for him, the <s>bhikṣu</s> who wishes it may accept it. Having accepted it, if it completes [his need], he should quickly make it up and wear it. If it does not complete [his need], that <s>bhikṣu</s> may store that robe-cloth for at most one month, provided there is an expectation of more robe-cloth, for the purpose of completing what is lacking. Should he store it beyond that — <s>Niḥsargikā Pātayantikā</s> 3.

children.text:
PrMoSū_NP.4:
yaḥ punar bhikṣur ajñātyā bhikṣuṇyā purāṇacīvaraṃ dhāvayed vā rañjayed vā ākoṭayed vā niḥsargikā pātayantik(ā) 4
children.translated_text: If a <s>bhikṣu</s> should have an unrelated <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> wash, dye, or beat an old robe — <s>Niḥsargikā Pātayantikā</s> 4.

children.text:
PrMoSū_NP.5:
yaḥ punar bhikṣur ajñātyā bhikṣuṇyāḥ santikāc cīvaraṃ pratigṛhṇīyād anyatra parivartakena niḥsargikā pātayantikā 5
children.translated_text: If a <s>bhikṣu</s> should accept a robe from an unrelated <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, except in exchange — <s>Niḥsargikā Pātayantikā</s> 5.

children.text:
PrMoSū_NP.6:
yaḥ punar bhikṣur ajñātiṃ gṛhapatiṃ gṛhapatipatnīṃ vā cīvaraṃ vijñāpayed anyatra samayād abhiniṣpanne cīvare niḥsargikā pātayantikā 6 tatrā(ya)ṃ samaya ācchinnacīvaro bhikṣuḥ syān naṣṭacīvaro (v)ā dagdhacīvaro (v)ā ūḍhacīvar(o vā ayaṃ) tatra samayaḥ
children.translated_text: If a <s>bhikṣu</s> should ask an unrelated householder or householder's wife for a robe, except at the proper occasion — <s>Niḥsargikā Pātayantikā</s> 6. The proper occasion here is: if a <s>bhikṣu</s>'s robe has been stolen, or lost, or burnt, or carried away by flood. This is the proper occasion.

children.text:
PrMoSū_NP.7:
ācchinnacīvareṇa bhikṣuṇā naṣṭacīvareṇa vā dagdhacīvareṇa vā ūḍhacīvareṇa vā ajñāti(ṃ g)ṛ(hapa)tiṃ gṛhapatipatnīṃ vā cīvaraṃ vijñā... (taṃ ced bhi)kṣu(ṃ) śrā(d)dh(o) gṛhapatir gṛhapatipatnī vā saṃbahulaiś cīvarai(ḥ) pravārayed ākāṃkṣamāṇena tena bhikṣuṇā sāntarottarapa(ra)ma(ṃ) tataś cīvaraṃ pratigṛhītavyaṃ tata uttaraṃ prati(gṛhṇīyān n)iḥsargikā pātayantikā 7
children.translated_text: If a <s>bhikṣu</s> whose robe has been stolen, lost, burnt, or carried away by flood is offered many robes by an unrelated householder or householder's wife, that <s>bhikṣu</s> wishing [more] should accept at most an upper and lower robe from them. Should he accept beyond that — <s>Niḥsargikā Pātayantikā</s> 7.

children.translated_text: If robe-fund materials are set aside by an unrelated householder or householder's wife for a [particular] <s>bhikṣu</s>, [thinking]: 'With these robe-fund materials I shall have such-and-such a robe made and shall clothe the <s>bhikṣu</s> named so-and-so' — if that <s>bhikṣu</s>, without having been previously invited, should approach that unrelated householder or householder's wife and, making some suggestion, should say: 'The robe-fund materials that were set aside by the venerable one for me — with those robe-fund materials, please have such-and-such a robe made and clothe the <s>bhikṣu</s> named so-and-so' — [if he says this] out of desire for something fine — <s>Niḥsargikā Pātayantikā</s> 8.

children.translated_text: If separate robe-fund materials are set aside by two unrelated householders or their wives for a [particular] <s>bhikṣu</s>, [thinking]: 'With these our robe-fund materials we shall each have such-and-such a robe made and shall clothe the <s>bhikṣu</s> named so-and-so, each with a separate robe' — if that <s>bhikṣu</s>, without having been previously invited, should approach those two unrelated householders or their wives and, making some suggestion, should say: 'Those robe-fund materials that were set aside by the venerable ones for me — with those robe-fund materials, please combine them and have such-and-such a robe made and clothe me with one robe' — [if he says this] out of desire for something fine — <s>Niḥsargikā Pātayantikā</s> 9.

children.translated_text: A <s>bhikṣu</s> who desires a robe should approach the steward (<s>vaiyyāpatyakara</s>) and remind him two or three times: 'I have need, O steward, of a robe.' If after reminding two or three times the robe should be obtained — that is proper.

PrMoSū_NP.11:

children.translated_text: <s>Niḥsargikā Pātayantikā</s> 11: If a <s>bhikṣu</s> should have a new rug made of silk — <s>Niḥsargikā Pātayantikā</s> 11.

children.text:
PrMoSū_NP.12:
yaḥ punar bhikṣuḥ śuddhakāḍānām eḍakalomnāṃ navaṃ saṃstaraṃ kārayen niḥsargikā pātayantikā 12
children.translated_text: <s>Niḥsargikā Pātayantikā</s> 12: If a <s>bhikṣu</s> should have a new rug made of pure black sheep's wool — <s>Niḥsargikā Pātayantikā</s> 12.

children.text:
PrMoSū_NP.13:
navaṃ punar bhikṣuṇā saṃstaraṃ kārayatā dvau bhāgau śuddhakāḍānām eḍakalomnām ādātavyau tṛtīyo 'vadātānāṃ caturtho gocarikānām anādāya ced bhikṣur dvau bhāgau śuddhakāḍānām eḍakalomnām tṛtīyam avadātānāṃ caturthaṃ gocarikānāṃ navaṃ saṃstaraṃ kārayet kalyāṇakāmatām upādāya niḥsargikā pātayantikā 13
children.translated_text: <s>Niḥsargikā Pātayantikā</s> 13: When a <s>bhikṣu</s> is having a new rug made, two parts of pure black sheep's wool are to be taken, the third of white, and the fourth of coarse [wool]. If a <s>bhikṣu</s>, without taking two parts of pure black sheep's wool,

children.translated_text: <s>Niḥsargikā Pātayantikā</s> 14: When a <s>bhikṣu</s> has had a new rug made, he must keep it for at least six years. children.translated_text: <s>Niḥsargikā Pātayantikā</s> 15: When a <s>bhikṣu</s> is having a new sitting-rug made, a piece from the border of an old sitting-rug measuring one <s>sugata</s>-span must be taken for the purpose of discoloring the new one. If a <s>bhikṣu</s>, without taking from the border of an old sitting-rug a piece of one <s>sugata</s>-span,

bhikṣoś ced adhvānamārgapratipannasyotpadyerann eḍakalomāni ākāṅkṣatā tena bhikṣuṇā pratigṛhītavyāni pratigṛhya yāvat triyojanaparamaṃ svayaṃ hartavyāny asati hartari tata uttaraṃ haren niḥsargikā pātayantikā 16
children.translated_text: <s>Niḥsargikā Pātayantikā</s> 16: If sheep's wool should arise [i.e., become available] for a <s>bhikṣu</s> who has set out on a road-journey, the <s>bhikṣu</s> who desires [it] may accept it. Having accepted it, he may carry it himself for a maximum of three <s>yojanas</s>. If there is no one to carry [it], should he carry it beyond that —

yaḥ punar bhikṣur ajñātyā bhikṣuṇyā eḍakalomāni dhāvayed vā rañjayed vā vijaṭayed vā niḥsargikā pātayantikā 17
children.translated_text: <s>Niḥsargikā Pātayantikā</s> 17: If a <s>bhikṣu</s> should have sheep's wool washed, or dyed, or carded by an unrelated <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> — <s>Niḥsargikā Pātayantikā</s> 17.

children.text:
PrMoSū_NP.18:
yaḥ punar bhikṣuḥ svahastaṃ rūpyam u(d)gṛhṇīyād vā udgrāhayed vā niḥsargikā (pātayantikā) 18
children.translated_text: <s>Niḥsargikā Pātayantikā</s> 18: If a <s>bhikṣu</s> should with his own hand pick up money (<s>rūpya</s>), or cause it to be picked up — <s>Niḥsargikā Pātayantikā</s> 18.

children.text:
PrMoSū_NP.19:
yaḥ punar bhikṣur nānāprakāraṃ rūpyavyavahāraṃ samāpadyeta niḥsargikā pātayantikā 19
children.translated_text: <s>Niḥsargikā Pātayantikā</s> 19: If a <s>bhikṣu</s> should engage in various kinds of transactions involving money (<s>rūpya</s>) — <s>Niḥsargikā Pātayantikā</s> 19.

children.text:
PrMoSū_NP.20 :
yaḥ punar bhikṣur nānāprakāraṃ krayavikrayaṃ samāpadyeta niḥsargi(kā pātayantikā) 20 //
children.translated_text: <s>Niḥsargikā Pātayantikā</s> 20: If a <s>bhikṣu</s> should engage in various kinds of buying and selling — <s>Niḥsargikā Pātayantikā</s> 20.

daśāhaparamaṃ bhikṣuṇā atiriktaṃ pātraṃ dhārayitavyaṃ tata uttaraṃ dhārayen niḥ(sa)r(gikā pātayantikā) 21
children.translated_text: <s>Niḥsargikā Pātayantikā</s> 21: A <s>bhikṣu</s> may keep an extra bowl for a maximum of ten days. Should he keep it beyond that — <s>Niḥsargikā Pātayantikā</s> 21.

children.translated_text: <s>Niḥsargikā Pātayantikā</s> 23: If a <s>bhikṣu</s> should have a robe woven by an unrelated weaver, having himself begged for the thread — <s>Niḥsargikā Pātayantikā</s> 23.
